CHAPTER 4 — कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत? (KASMAT KIM SHIKSHET) — What should one learn, and from whom?

Introduction — कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत?

The title of this lesson is a question: कस्मात् (kasmat = from whom / from what) किम् (kim = what) शिक्षेत् (shikshet = should one learn)? — 'From whom should one learn what?' The Sanskrit tradition gives a bold and beautiful answer: a wise person (धीमान्) learns good qualities from EVERY source — from animals, from birds, from rivers and trees, and from people high and low. Nothing is too small to teach us; a single virtue found even in a humble creature is worth taking. The famous saying 'गुणाः पूजास्थानं गुणिषु न च लिङ्गं न च वयः' reminds us that it is the QUALITY that deserves honour, not the size, age or rank of the one who has it. In this lesson (NIOS Secondary Sanskrit, Course 209) we study well-known public-domain नीति-verses (from the Chanakya-niti tradition) that tell us to learn one quality from the lion, one from the heron, four from the cock, five from the crow, six from the dog and three from the donkey — twenty virtues in all — and we draw grammar (सन्धि, विभक्ति, धातुरूप) from the verses.

Why learn from animals? (पशुभ्यः किमर्थं शिक्षेत?)

Animals act by their nature (स्वभावः). The lion hunts with total effort, the heron waits with perfect patience, the dog is loyal to the end, the donkey carries its load without complaint. Human beings have reason (बुद्धिः), so we can OBSERVE these natural virtues and CHOOSE to make them our own. The ancient teachers therefore turned the animal world into a classroom. This does not mean we copy an animal in every way; we take only the ONE good quality (गुणः) it shows most clearly, and leave the rest. This is the art of the wise: 'सर्वतः सारमादद्यात्' — one should gather the essence (सार) from everywhere, as a bee gathers honey from many flowers.

The Master Verse (मूल-श्लोकः)

सिंहादेकं बकादेकं शिक्षेच्चत्वारि कुक्कुटात् ।
वायसात् पञ्च शिक्षेच्च षट् शुनस्त्रीणि गर्दभात् ॥

शब्दार्थ: सिंहात् = from the lion; एकम् = one (quality); बकात् = from the heron/crane; शिक्षेत् = one should learn; चत्वारि = four; कुक्कुटात् = from the cock/rooster; वायसात् = from the crow; पञ्च = five; च = and; षट् = six; शुनः = from the dog; त्रीणि = three; गर्दभात् = from the donkey.
Translation: One (quality) should be learned from the lion, one from the heron, four from the cock, five from the crow, six from the dog, and three from the donkey.
Theme / Moral: A single verse becomes a map of twenty virtues. It teaches the deepest lesson of all — that a good student is a life-long collector of good qualities, ready to learn from any teacher, however humble.

One quality from the lion (सिंहात् एकम्)

प्रभूतं कार्यमल्पं वा यन्नरः कर्तुमिच्छति ।
सर्वारम्भेण तत्कार्यं सिंहादेकं प्रचक्षते ॥

शब्दार्थ: प्रभूतम् = great, large; कार्यम् = task, work; अल्पम् = small; वा = or; यत् = which; नरः = a man; कर्तुम् = to do; इच्छति = wishes; सर्वारम्भेण = with all one's effort, with full endeavour; तत् = that; प्रचक्षते = (the wise) call/declare; सिंहात् एकम् = the one (thing) from the lion.
Translation: Whatever task a man wishes to do, whether great or small, he should do that task with all his might — this one (quality) is said to be learned from the lion.
Moral: The lion never hunts half-heartedly, even for a small animal. So too, we should put our WHOLE effort (सर्वारम्भ) into every task, big or small. This single virtue — wholehearted effort — is the lion's gift to the wise.

One quality from the heron (बकात् एकम्)

इन्द्रियाणि च संयम्य बकवत्पण्डितो नरः ।
देशकालबलं ज्ञात्वा सर्वकार्याणि साधयेत् ॥

शब्दार्थ: इन्द्रियाणि = the senses; संयम्य = having controlled; बकवत् = like a heron; पण्डितः = a wise man; नरः = a person; देशकालबलम् = place, time and (one's own) strength; ज्ञात्वा = having known; सर्वकार्याणि = all tasks; साधयेत् = should accomplish.
Translation: Controlling his senses like a heron (that stands still and waits), the wise man, having judged place, time and his own strength, should accomplish all his tasks.
Moral: The heron stands motionless at the water's edge, its senses gathered and focused, and strikes only at the right moment. From it we learn concentration (एकाग्रता) and the wisdom of acting at the proper place and time (देश-काल).

Six qualities from the dog (श्वानात् षट्)

बह्वाशी स्वल्पसन्तुष्टः सुनिद्रो लघुचेतनः ।
स्वामिभक्तश्च शूरश्च षडेते श्वानतो गुणाः ॥

शब्दार्थ: बह्वाशी = able to eat much (when food is there); स्वल्पसन्तुष्टः = content with little (when it is not); सुनिद्रः = a sound sleeper; लघुचेतनः = yet easily awakened, alert; स्वामिभक्तः = devoted/loyal to its master; शूरः = brave; षट् एते = these six; श्वानतः = from the dog; गुणाः = qualities.
Translation: Able to eat much yet content with little, a sound sleeper who is nevertheless quick to wake, loyal to its master, and brave — these six are the (good) qualities (to be learned) from the dog.
Moral: The dog teaches contentment (सन्तोष), alertness even at rest, loyalty (स्वामिभक्ति) and courage (शौर्य). A student who is thankful, watchful, faithful and brave has learned the dog's whole lesson.

Three qualities from the donkey (गर्दभात् त्रीणि)

सुश्रान्तोऽपि वहेद्भारं शीतोष्णं न च पश्यति ।
सन्तुष्टश्चरते नित्यं त्रीणि शिक्षेच्च गर्दभात् ॥

शब्दार्थ: सुश्रान्तः = very tired; अपि = even; वहेत् = should carry; भारम् = the burden, load; शीतोष्णम् = cold and heat; न च पश्यति = does not (even) regard/mind; सन्तुष्टः = content; चरते = moves about, lives; नित्यम् = always; त्रीणि = three; गर्दभात् = from the donkey.
Translation: Even when very tired it carries its burden; it does not mind cold or heat; it is always content — these three (qualities) one should learn from the donkey.
Moral: The humble donkey teaches perseverance (धैर्य / सहनशीलता), endurance of hardship, and contentment. It reminds us that a great quality can shine even in the lowliest creature — so we must never despise any teacher.

The cock and the crow (कुक्कुटः वायसश्च)

The verses also praise four qualities of the cock (कुक्कुटः) — rising alert at the right time (प्रत्युत्थानम्), courage in a fair fight (युद्धम्), sharing food with one's kinsmen (संविभागं बन्धुषु), and eating what one has earned by one's own effort. From the crow (वायसः) the tradition lists five — boldness (धार्ष्ट्यम्), storing/saving at the proper time (काले संग्रहम्), constant watchfulness (अप्रमत्तता), careful discernment about whom to trust (अविश्वासः), and keeping one's private matters private. Thus the little cock teaches punctuality and generosity, and the clever crow teaches foresight and caution.

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar from the verses (English explanation, Devanagari examples)

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — the joining of sounds). When two sounds meet, Sanskrit often joins and changes them.
  • व्यञ्जन-सन्धि (consonant sandhi): सिंहात् + एकम् = सिंहादेकम् (the त् at the end of सिंहात् softens to द् before the vowel). Split it back as सिंहात् + एकम्.
  • श्चुत्व-सन्धि: शिक्षेत् + चत्वारि = शिक्षेच्चत्वारि, and शिक्षेत् + च = शिक्षेच्च (त् before च becomes च्). Split back as शिक्षेत् + चत्वारि.
  • विसर्ग-सन्धि (visarga sandhi): शुनः + त्रीणि = शुनस्त्रीणि (the visarga ः before त becomes स्); सन्तुष्टः + चरते = सन्तुष्टश्चरते (ः before च becomes श्).
  • विसर्ग/गुण-सन्धि with अवग्रह: सुश्रान्तः + अपि = सुश्रान्तोऽपि (अः + अ = ओ followed by the sign ऽ, called अवग्रह, marking the dropped अ).
Being able to SPLIT a sandhi (सन्धि-विच्छेद) back into its parts is a key reading skill.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). The most important case in these verses is the पञ्चमी (ablative), which means 'from':
  • पञ्चमी (ablative, 'from'): सिंहात् 'from the lion', बकात् 'from the heron', कुक्कुटात् 'from the cock', वायसात् 'from the crow', गर्दभात् 'from the donkey'. The ending -आत् marks 'from'. (The word शुनः 'from the dog' is the पञ्चमी of the irregular noun श्वन्; श्वानतः, with the ending -तः, also means 'from the dog'.)
  • द्वितीया (accusative, object): एकम्, चत्वारि, पञ्च, त्रीणि, भारम्, कार्यम् — 'one/four/five/three (qualities)', 'the burden', 'the task', which are what is learned or done.
  • तृतीया (instrumental, 'by/with'): सर्वारम्भेण 'with all effort'.
  • सप्तमी (locative, 'in/among'): बन्धुषु 'among kinsmen'.
  • प्रथमा (nominative, subject): नरः 'a man', पण्डितः 'the wise man', गुणाः 'the qualities'.

(C) धातुरूप (verb-form) and सङ्ख्या (numbers). The verb शिक्षेत् ('one should learn') is the विधिलिङ् (potential/optative mood) of the root शिक्ष् (to learn); the विधिलिङ् expresses 'should' or 'ought to'. The same mood appears in वहेत् 'should carry' and साधयेत् 'should accomplish'. The verse also drills the neuter numbers: एकम् (1), त्रीणि (3), चत्वारि (4), पञ्च (5), षट् (6). Notice that एक, त्रि and चतुर् change their form to agree with the (neuter) word 'quality', giving एकम्, त्रीणि, चत्वारि, while पञ्च and षट् stay the same.

(D) शब्दरूप (declension — worked example). The masculine a-stem सिंह declines in the प्रथमा as सिंहः (one) / सिंहौ (two) / सिंहाः (many), and in the पञ्चमी (ablative, 'from') as सिंहात् (from one) / सिंहाभ्याम् (from two) / सिंहेभ्यः (from many). In the master verse सिंहात्, बकात्, कुक्कुटात्, वायसात् and गर्दभात् are all singular ablatives — 'from the lion', 'from the heron', and so on.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you learned to answer the question कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत — 'from whom should one learn what?' The wise take good qualities from every source. The master verse सिंहादेकं बकादेकम्... lists twenty virtues: one from the lion (wholehearted effort), one from the heron (self-control and right timing), four from the cock (alert rising, courage, sharing with kin, honest earning), five from the crow (boldness, timely saving, watchfulness, discernment, privacy), six from the dog (contentment, alertness even in sleep, loyalty, courage), and three from the donkey (perseverance, endurance of cold and heat, contentment). For each you studied the शब्दार्थ, an English translation and the moral. Finally you drew grammar from the verses: व्यञ्जन-, श्चुत्व- and विसर्ग-सन्धि (and how to split them), the पञ्चमी 'from' case with the other common विभक्तिs, the विधिलिङ् verb शिक्षेत् 'should learn', the neuter numbers, and the शब्दरूप of the a-stem सिंह. Memorise the master verse — it is a pocket handbook of good character.

topics.name: कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत? — Learning Good Qualities from All Sources
topics.description: The theme of the lesson: from whom should one learn what? The Sanskrit idea that a wise person gathers good qualities (गुणाः) from every source — animals, birds, nature and people — because it is the virtue, not the rank of its owner, that deserves honour.

topics.description: Translating the verses into simple English and answering comprehension questions — identifying the source, the number of qualities, key word meanings, the case of a word and the moral of a given verse.

key_takeaways: कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत — the wise learn good qualities from every source; honour the virtue, not its owner's rank.
The master verse सिंहादेकं बकादेकम्... maps twenty virtues onto six creatures.
Lion 1, heron 1, cock 4, crow 5, dog 6, donkey 3 — remember the counts to recall all twenty qualities.
The lion teaches wholehearted effort (सर्वारम्भ); the dog teaches contentment, loyalty and courage; the donkey teaches perseverance.
Even a humble creature like the donkey can teach a great virtue, so never despise any teacher.
व्यञ्जन-, श्चुत्व- and विसर्ग-सन्धि join sounds where words meet (सिंहात् + एकम् = सिंहादेकम्); splitting them is सन्धि-विच्छेद.
The पञ्चमी ending -आत् means 'from' (सिंहात्, गर्दभात्), and the विधिलिङ् शिक्षेत् means 'one should learn'.

glossary.definition: From whom / from what (पञ्चमी of किम्); the opening word of the lesson's title-question कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत.
One should learn; the विधिलिङ् (mood of 'should/ought') of the root शिक्ष् (to learn).
A good quality or virtue; the thing to be gathered from every source (plural गुणाः).
The lion; teaches the one quality of doing every task with full effort (सर्वारम्भ).
The heron/crane; teaches self-control of the senses and acting at the right place and time.
The cock/rooster; teaches four qualities — alert rising, courage, sharing with kin, and honest earning.
The crow; teaches five qualities — boldness, timely saving, watchfulness, discernment and privacy.
The dog; teaches six qualities — contentment, alertness even in sleep, loyalty (स्वामिभक्ति) and courage. शुनः / श्वानतः = 'from the dog'.
The donkey; teaches three qualities — perseverance in carrying its burden, endurance of cold and heat, and contentment.
With all one's effort, with full endeavour (तृतीया); the lion's way of doing every task.
Devoted or loyal to one's master; a chief virtue of the dog.
Content, satisfied; a virtue shared by the dog (स्वल्पसन्तुष्ट) and the donkey.
The ablative case, meaning 'from'; ending -आत् as in सिंहात्, बकात्, गर्दभात्.
The joining/merging of sounds where two words meet, e.g. सिंहात् + एकम् = सिंहादेकम्.
The verb-mood expressing 'should/ought'; e.g. शिक्षेत् 'should learn', वहेत् 'should carry'.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत? (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 4)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the verses in the lesson where needed.

questions.question: Write the master verse 'सिंहादेकं बकादेकम्...' in Devanagari and translate it into simple English.
questions.answer: सिंहादेकं बकादेकं शिक्षेच्चत्वारि कुक्कुटात्। वायसात् पञ्च शिक्षेच्च षट् शुनस्त्रीणि गर्दभात्॥ Translation: One quality should be learned from the lion, one from the heron, four from the cock, five from the crow, six from the dog, and three from the donkey.
questions.explanation: Recall of the master verse plus its full translation; twenty qualities in all.

questions.question: State how many qualities are to be learned from each of the six creatures.
questions.answer: Lion (सिंह) 1, heron (बक) 1, cock (कुक्कुट) 4, crow (वायस) 5, dog (श्वान) 6, donkey (गर्दभ) 3 — twenty qualities in all.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: सिंहात्, गर्दभात्, भारम्, गुणाः.
questions.answer: सिंहात् = from the lion; गर्दभात् = from the donkey; भारम् = the burden/load; गुणाः = qualities/virtues.
questions.explanation: सिंहात् and गर्दभात् are पञ्चमी (ablative) 'from'; भारम् is द्वितीया (object).

questions.question: What one quality does the lion teach, and how should a student apply it?
questions.answer: The lion teaches doing every task, great or small, with all one's effort (सर्वारम्भेण). A student should apply this by studying and working wholeheartedly, never doing any task half-heartedly.
questions.explanation: From प्रभूतं कार्यमल्पं वा...; the virtue is wholehearted effort.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) सिंहादेकम् (b) शिक्षेच्च.
questions.answer: (a) सिंहादेकम् = सिंहात् + एकम् (त् softens to द् before the vowel, व्यञ्जन-सन्धि). (b) शिक्षेच्च = शिक्षेत् + च (त् before च becomes च्, श्चुत्व-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form back into its words is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: Take the dog verse 'बह्वाशी स्वल्पसन्तुष्टः सुनिद्रो लघुचेतनः, स्वामिभक्तश्च शूरश्च षडेते श्वानतो गुणाः'. Give its word meanings and explain the six qualities of the dog.
questions.answer:
शब्दार्थ: बह्वाशी = able to eat much; स्वल्पसन्तुष्टः = content with little; सुनिद्रः = a sound sleeper; लघुचेतनः = yet easily awakened, alert; स्वामिभक्तः = loyal to its master; शूरः = brave; षट् एते = these six; श्वानतः = from the dog; गुणाः = qualities.
Explanation: The dog shows six virtues worth learning. (1) It can eat a lot when food is plentiful but (2) is content with little when it is not, teaching contentment. (3) It sleeps soundly yet (4) wakes at the slightest sound, teaching alertness even at rest. (5) It is deeply loyal to its master (स्वामिभक्ति), and (6) it is brave (शूर) in facing danger. A student who is thankful, watchful, faithful and courageous has learned the dog's whole lesson.
questions.explanation: Word meanings plus explanation of contentment, alertness, loyalty and courage.

questions.question: Explain the theme कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत and why the ancients told us to learn even from humble animals. How can you practise this idea?
questions.answer:
कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत means 'from whom should one learn what?' The Sanskrit answer is that a wise person gathers good qualities (गुणाः) from every source — animals, birds, nature and people alike — because it is the virtue, not the size, age or rank of its owner, that deserves honour. Animals act by their nature: the lion with full effort, the dog with loyalty, the donkey with endurance. Human beings, having reason, can observe these natural virtues and choose to make them their own, taking only the good quality and leaving the rest, as a bee gathers honey from many flowers.
A student can practise this by watching for a good quality in everyone and everything — a hardworking classmate, a patient elder, a loyal pet — and by trying to imitate that one virtue. This keeps the mind humble and always learning.
questions.explanation: Theme, reason for learning from animals, and practical application.

questions.question: Explain the three qualities taught by the donkey (गर्दभ) from the verse 'सुश्रान्तोऽपि वहेद्भारम्...'.
questions.answer: The donkey teaches three qualities: (1) perseverance — even when very tired (सुश्रान्तः) it still carries its burden (वहेद्भारम्); (2) endurance — it does not mind cold or heat (शीतोष्णं न च पश्यति); and (3) contentment — it always stays satisfied (सन्तुष्टश्चरते नित्यम्).
questions.explanation: Perseverance, endurance of hardship, and contentment.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its meaning-role for each: सिंहात्, बन्धुषु.
questions.answer: सिंहात् = पञ्चमी (ablative) → 'from the lion' (the source one learns from). बन्धुषु = सप्तमी (locative) → 'among the kinsmen' (where the cock shares its food).
questions.explanation: पञ्चमी shows source ('from'); सप्तमी shows location ('in/among').

questions.question: What does the heron (बक) teach in the verse 'इन्द्रियाणि च संयम्य बकवत्पण्डितो नरः...'? Give its moral.
questions.answer: The heron teaches the wise man to control his senses (इन्द्रियसंयम) like a still, focused heron, and to accomplish his tasks only after judging the right place, time and his own strength (देशकालबलं ज्ञात्वा). The moral is concentration and acting at the proper time.

questions.question: What does the title 'कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत' mean, and what is its central idea?
questions.answer: It means 'from whom should one learn what?' Its central idea is that a wise person gathers good qualities from every source — animals, nature and people — because virtue is worth taking wherever it is found.
questions.explanation: Title meaning plus the theme of learning from all sources.

questions.question: Give two reasons why the tradition asks us to learn good qualities from animals.
questions.answer: (1) Animals show certain virtues very clearly by their nature — the lion its effort, the dog its loyalty, the donkey its endurance. (2) Having reason, humans can observe these natural virtues and choose to make them their own, taking the good quality and leaving the rest.
questions.explanation: Animals model virtue; humans can consciously imitate it.

questions.question: Explain the idea that a wise person is a 'collector of virtues'. Use the bee image from the lesson.
questions.answer: A wise person does not depend on one teacher only. Just as a bee flies from flower to flower gathering a little honey from each, the wise person moves through life gathering a good quality from each person, animal or situation — effort from the lion, patience from the heron, loyalty from the dog. Over time these small gatherings build a rich, virtuous character. So the wise are life-long collectors of virtues (गुणग्राहिणः).
questions.explanation: The bee simile (सर्वतः सारमादद्यात्) applied to character-building.

questions.question: Write the master verse 'सिंहादेकं बकादेकम्...' in Devanagari.
questions.answer: सिंहादेकं बकादेकं शिक्षेच्चत्वारि कुक्कुटात्। वायसात् पञ्च शिक्षेच्च षट् शुनस्त्रीणि गर्दभात्॥
questions.explanation: Recall of the master verse.

questions.question: List how many qualities are learned from each of the six creatures.
questions.answer: Lion (सिंह) = 1; heron (बक) = 1; cock (कुक्कुट) = 4; crow (वायस) = 5; dog (श्वान) = 6; donkey (गर्दभ) = 3. Total = 20 qualities.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the lion verse 'प्रभूतं कार्यमल्पं वा यन्नरः कर्तुमिच्छति, सर्वारम्भेण तत्कार्यं सिंहादेकं प्रचक्षते'.
questions.answer: Whatever task a man wishes to do, whether it is great (प्रभूतम्) or small (अल्पम्), he should do it with all his effort (सर्वारम्भेण). This one virtue — putting one's whole strength into every task — is said to be learned from the lion, who hunts wholeheartedly even for small prey.
questions.explanation: Wholehearted effort is the lion's single lesson.

questions.question: What does the heron (बक) teach? Explain in one or two sentences.
questions.answer: The heron teaches self-control of the senses (इन्द्रियसंयम) and acting only after judging the right place, time and one's own strength (देशकालबलं ज्ञात्वा). Like a still, focused heron waiting to strike, the wise person concentrates and acts at the proper moment.
questions.explanation: Concentration and right timing.

questions.question: Name and explain the six qualities of the dog from 'बह्वाशी स्वल्पसन्तुष्टः...'.
questions.answer: The dog's six qualities are: (1) बह्वाशी — able to eat much when food is plenty; (2) स्वल्पसन्तुष्टः — yet content with little; (3) सुनिद्रः — a sound sleeper; (4) लघुचेतनः — yet quick to wake, alert; (5) स्वामिभक्तः — loyal to its master; (6) शूरः — brave. Together they teach contentment, alertness even at rest, loyalty and courage.
questions.explanation: Six virtues: contentment, alertness, loyalty, courage.

questions.question: Explain the donkey verse 'सुश्रान्तोऽपि वहेद्भारं शीतोष्णं न च पश्यति, सन्तुष्टश्चरते नित्यम्'.
questions.answer: Even when very tired the donkey still carries its burden; it does not mind cold or heat; and it always stays content. Thus the donkey teaches perseverance, endurance of hardship, and contentment.
questions.explanation: Perseverance, endurance and contentment.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: सिंहात्, बकात्, गर्दभात्.
questions.answer: सिंहात् = from the lion; बकात् = from the heron; गर्दभात् = from the donkey. (All are पञ्चमी 'from'.)
questions.explanation: Ablative forms meaning 'from'.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: भारम्, शूरः, सन्तुष्टः.
questions.answer: भारम् = burden/load; शूरः = brave; सन्तुष्टः = content/satisfied.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from the dog and donkey verses.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: गुणाः, बन्धुषु, नरः.
questions.answer: गुणाः = qualities/virtues; बन्धुषु = among kinsmen/relatives; नरः = a man/person.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from the verses.

questions.question: What life-lessons can a student take from the lion and the dog?
questions.answer: From the lion a student learns to do every task, big or small, with full effort (सर्वारम्भेण) — studying and working wholeheartedly. From the dog a student learns contentment with little, alertness even while resting, loyalty and gratitude to teachers and parents, and courage in facing difficulties. Together they build a hardworking, faithful and brave character.
questions.explanation: Effort from the lion; contentment, loyalty, courage from the dog.

questions.question: How does the donkey teach perseverance and contentment?
questions.answer: The donkey carries its burden even when very tired (सुश्रान्तोऽपि वहेद्भारम्) and does not mind cold or heat — this teaches perseverance and endurance. It also lives always content (सन्तुष्टश्चरते नित्यम्) — this teaches contentment. A student should likewise keep working without complaint and be satisfied with what they have.
questions.explanation: Endurance of hardship plus contentment.

questions.question: Which quality of the crow is useful for planning and saving? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: The crow's quality of 'storing/saving at the proper time' (काले संग्रहम्), along with its constant watchfulness (अप्रमत्तता), is useful for planning and saving. It teaches us to gather and keep resources at the right time and to stay alert, so we are prepared for the future.
questions.explanation: Timely saving and foresight.

questions.question: 'A good quality can be learned even from a humble source.' Discuss this idea with an example from the lesson.
questions.answer: The lesson tells us to honour the quality (गुण), not the rank of its owner. Even the lowly donkey — a creature many look down upon — teaches three great virtues: perseverance, endurance and contentment. If such wisdom lives in a donkey, then no source of virtue is too small. So we should keep our minds humble and be ready to learn a good quality from anyone, whether great or lowly.
questions.explanation: Applies 'honour the virtue, not the rank' with the donkey example.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) सिंहादेकम् (b) शिक्षेच्चत्वारि.
questions.answer: (a) सिंहादेकम् = सिंहात् + एकम् (त् → द् before a vowel, व्यञ्जन-सन्धि). (b) शिक्षेच्चत्वारि = शिक्षेत् + चत्वारि (त् before च → च्, श्चुत्व-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting joined forms back into words.

questions.question: Join by sandhi: (a) शुनः + त्रीणि (b) सन्तुष्टः + चरते.
questions.answer: (a) शुनः + त्रीणि = शुनस्त्रीणि (visarga ः → स् before त). (b) सन्तुष्टः + चरते = सन्तुष्टश्चरते (visarga ः → श् before च).
questions.explanation: विसर्ग-सन्धि joins.

questions.question: What is व्यञ्जन-सन्धि? Give one example from the verses.
questions.answer: व्यञ्जन-सन्धि is the joining rule in which a final consonant changes when it meets the next sound. Example from the verse: सिंहात् + एकम् = सिंहादेकम्, where the final त् softens to द् before the vowel ए.
questions.explanation: Consonant sandhi with the सिंहादेकम् example.

questions.question: Name the विभक्ति and role of सिंहात् and बन्धुषु.
questions.answer: सिंहात् = पञ्चमी (ablative), meaning 'from the lion' — it shows the source of learning. बन्धुषु = सप्तमी (locative), meaning 'among the kinsmen' — it shows the place/among whom the cock shares its food.
questions.explanation: Ablative 'from' and locative 'among'.

questions.question: Write the शब्दरूप of सिंह in the पञ्चमी विभक्ति (all three numbers).
questions.answer: पञ्चमी: एकवचन सिंहात् (from one lion), द्विवचन सिंहाभ्याम् (from two), बहुवचन सिंहेभ्यः (from many).
questions.explanation: Ablative declension of the a-stem सिंह.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'षट् शुनस्त्रीणि गर्दभात्'.
questions.answer: 'Six (qualities) from the dog, and three from the donkey.' षट् = six, शुनः = from the dog, त्रीणि = three, गर्दभात् = from the donkey.
questions.explanation: Simple translation of the second half-line.

questions.question: Explain the theme 'कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत' and why the ancients told us to learn from animals. How can a student practise this idea?
questions.answer:
कस्मात् किं शिक्षेत means 'from whom should one learn what?' The Sanskrit answer is that the wise gather good qualities (गुणाः) from every source — animals, birds, nature and people — because it is the virtue, not the size, age or rank of its owner, that deserves honour. The ancients turned the animal world into a classroom because animals show virtues clearly by their nature: the lion its full effort, the heron its patience, the dog its loyalty, the donkey its endurance. Human beings have reason, so they can observe these virtues and choose to make them their own, taking only the good quality and leaving the rest — as a bee gathers honey from many flowers.
A student can practise this by watching for a good quality in everyone and everything around them — a hardworking classmate, a patient elder, a faithful pet — and by trying to imitate that one virtue. This keeps the mind humble and always learning.
questions.explanation: Theme, reason for learning from animals, and practical application.

questions.question: Write the master verse and list all twenty qualities by their source (as given in the lesson).
questions.answer:
Verse: सिंहादेकं बकादेकं शिक्षेच्चत्वारि कुक्कुटात्। वायसात् पञ्च शिक्षेच्च षट् शुनस्त्रीणि गर्दभात्॥
Qualities by source: Lion (1) — wholehearted effort in every task. Heron (1) — control of the senses and acting at the right place and time. Cock (4) — alert rising at the right time, courage, sharing food with kinsmen, and honest earning. Crow (5) — boldness, timely saving, constant watchfulness, careful discernment about whom to trust, and privacy in personal matters. Dog (6) — eating much yet content with little, sound sleep yet quick to wake, loyalty to master, and courage. Donkey (3) — carrying the burden untiringly, enduring cold and heat, and staying always content. In all, twenty virtues.
questions.explanation: Verse plus the full list of twenty qualities.

questions.question: Take the dog verse 'बह्वाशी स्वल्पसन्तुष्टः सुनिद्रो लघुचेतनः, स्वामिभक्तश्च शूरश्च षडेते श्वानतो गुणाः'. Give its word meanings and full explanation.
questions.answer:
शब्दार्थ: बह्वाशी = able to eat much; स्वल्पसन्तुष्टः = content with little; सुनिद्रः = a sound sleeper; लघुचेतनः = yet easily awakened, alert; स्वामिभक्तः = loyal to its master; शूरः = brave; षट् एते = these six; श्वानतः = from the dog; गुणाः = qualities.
Explanation: The verse lists six virtues of the dog worth learning. The dog can eat a great deal when food is plentiful, yet it is happily content with little when food is scarce — this teaches contentment and adaptability. It sleeps soundly but wakes at the slightest sound — this teaches alertness even at rest. It is deeply devoted to its master (स्वामिभक्ति) and brave in facing danger. A student who is thankful and adaptable, watchful, faithful to teachers and parents, and courageous in difficulty has learned all six of the dog's qualities.
questions.explanation: Word meanings plus explanation of the six virtues.

questions.question: Discuss the qualities we should learn from the lion, the heron and the donkey, and explain how a student can apply each in daily life.
questions.answer:
Lion: it teaches doing every task, great or small, with all one's effort (सर्वारम्भेण). A student applies this by giving full attention and effort to every subject and chore, never working half-heartedly.
Heron: it teaches control of the senses and acting after judging place, time and strength (देशकालबलं ज्ञात्वा). A student applies this by concentrating during study, avoiding distractions, and planning tasks for the right time.
Donkey: it teaches perseverance (carrying its load even when tired), endurance of cold and heat, and contentment. A student applies this by continuing to work without complaint even when tired, bearing small hardships patiently, and being satisfied with what they have.
Together these three sources build a character that is hardworking, focused and steady — exactly the qualities a good student needs.
questions.explanation: Three sources, their virtues, and practical student applications.

questions.question: Compare the qualities of the dog and the donkey as taught in the verses.
questions.answer: Both the dog and the donkey teach contentment: the dog is स्वल्पसन्तुष्ट (content with little) and the donkey is सन्तुष्टश्चरते नित्यम् (always content). Beyond that, their lessons differ. The dog adds alertness (सुनिद्रो लघुचेतनः — sound sleep yet quick to wake), loyalty to its master (स्वामिभक्ति), and courage (शूरः) — six qualities in all. The donkey adds perseverance (carrying its burden even when tired) and endurance of cold and heat — three qualities in all. So while both teach contentment, the dog especially teaches alertness, loyalty and bravery, and the donkey especially teaches patient endurance and untiring effort. Both remind us that great virtues can be found in ordinary creatures.
questions.explanation: Shared virtue (contentment) plus each animal's distinct lessons.

questions.question: Explain सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद with four examples taken from the verses of this chapter.
questions.answer:
सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; सन्धि-विच्छेद is splitting such a joined form back into its separate words. Examples from the verses:
1. सिंहात् + एकम् = सिंहादेकम् (त् → द् before a vowel, व्यञ्जन-सन्धि).
2. शिक्षेत् + चत्वारि = शिक्षेच्चत्वारि (त् before च → च्, श्चुत्व-सन्धि).
3. शुनः + त्रीणि = शुनस्त्रीणि (visarga ः → स् before त, विसर्ग-सन्धि).
4. सुश्रान्तः + अपि = सुश्रान्तोऽपि (अः + अ → ओ with the sign ऽ, अवग्रह).
Being able both to join (सन्धि) and to split (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is essential for reading Sanskrit verses correctly.
questions.explanation: Definition plus four worked examples with their rules.

questions.question: Explain the पञ्चमी विभक्ति ('from') and the विधिलिङ् verb शिक्षेत् using examples from the verses.
questions.answer:
The पञ्चमी विभक्ति (ablative case) shows the source, and is translated 'from'. Its a-stem singular ending is -आत्. In the master verse it appears many times: सिंहात् 'from the lion', बकात् 'from the heron', कुक्कुटात् 'from the cock', वायसात् 'from the crow', गर्दभात् 'from the donkey'. (The form शुनः 'from the dog' is the पञ्चमी of the irregular noun श्वन्.)
The verb शिक्षेत् 'one should learn' is the विधिलिङ् (potential/optative mood) of the root शिक्ष्. The विधिलिङ् expresses duty or advice — 'should' or 'ought to'. The same mood appears in वहेत् 'should carry' and साधयेत् 'should accomplish'. So the verse literally advises: 'one SHOULD learn one quality FROM the lion...', using the ablative for the source and the विधिलिङ् for the advice.
questions.explanation: Ablative 'from' with verse examples plus the विधिलिङ् mood.

questions.question: Translate the master verse 'सिंहादेकं बकादेकं शिक्षेच्चत्वारि कुक्कुटात्, वायसात् पञ्च शिक्षेच्च षट् शुनस्त्रीणि गर्दभात्' and explain it.
questions.answer:
Translation: 'One (quality) should be learned from the lion, one from the heron, four from the cock; five from the crow, six from the dog, and three from the donkey.'
Explanation: The verse is a compact map of twenty virtues. It advises a wise person to take one good quality from the lion (wholehearted effort), one from the heron (self-control and right timing), four from the cock (alertness, courage, sharing, honest earning), five from the crow (boldness, timely saving, watchfulness, discernment, privacy), six from the dog (contentment, alertness, loyalty, courage) and three from the donkey (perseverance, endurance, contentment). Its deeper message is that a good student learns virtue from every source, however humble.
questions.explanation: Full translation plus explanation of the twenty-virtue message.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
सिंहादेकं बकादेकं शिक्षेच्चत्वारि कुक्कुटात्।
वायसात् पञ्च शिक्षेच्च षट् शुनस्त्रीणि गर्दभात्॥
(a) How many qualities should one learn from the lion? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'गर्दभात्'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'सिंहादेकम्'. (d) What is the overall theme of the verse?
questions.answer: (a) One quality from the lion (सिंहादेकम्). (b) गर्दभात् = 'from the donkey' (पञ्चमी/ablative). (c) सिंहादेकम् = सिंहात् + एकम्. (d) Theme: a wise person should learn good qualities from every source — twenty virtues from six creatures.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: count, word meaning, sandhi split, theme.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
प्रभूतं कार्यमल्पं वा यन्नरः कर्तुमिच्छति।
सर्वारम्भेण तत्कार्यं सिंहादेकं प्रचक्षते॥
(a) A task may be great or what? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'सर्वारम्भेण'. (c) In which विभक्ति is 'सिंहात्'? (d) What lesson does the lion teach?
questions.answer: (a) A task may be great (प्रभूतम्) or small (अल्पम्). (b) सर्वारम्भेण = 'with all one's effort'. (c) सिंहात् is पञ्चमी (ablative) — 'from the lion'. (d) Lesson: do every task, big or small, with your whole effort.
questions.explanation: Comprehension on the lion's wholehearted effort.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
बह्वाशी स्वल्पसन्तुष्टः सुनिद्रो लघुचेतनः।
स्वामिभक्तश्च शूरश्च षडेते श्वानतो गुणाः॥
(a) Name any two qualities of the dog. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'स्वामिभक्तः'. (c) How many qualities does the verse count? (d) What lesson can a student take from the dog?
questions.answer: (a) Any two of: content with little (स्वल्पसन्तुष्ट), alert even in sleep (सुनिद्रो लघुचेतनः), loyal (स्वामिभक्त), brave (शूर). (b) स्वामिभक्तः = loyal/devoted to the master. (c) Six qualities (षट्). (d) Lesson: be content, alert, loyal to teachers and parents, and brave.
questions.explanation: Comprehension on the dog's six qualities.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
सुश्रान्तोऽपि वहेद्भारं शीतोष्णं न च पश्यति।
सन्तुष्टश्चरते नित्यं त्रीणि शिक्षेच्च गर्दभात्॥
(a) What does the donkey carry even when tired? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'शीतोष्णम्'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'सुश्रान्तोऽपि'. (d) What is the moral of the verse?
questions.answer: (a) It carries its burden (भारम्) even when tired. (b) शीतोष्णम् = cold and heat. (c) सुश्रान्तोऽपि = सुश्रान्तः + अपि. (d) Moral: learn perseverance, endurance of hardship, and contentment from the donkey.
questions.explanation: Comprehension with a sandhi split; the donkey's three virtues.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
इन्द्रियाणि च संयम्य बकवत्पण्डितो नरः।
देशकालबलं ज्ञात्वा सर्वकार्याणि साधयेत्॥
(a) What should the wise man control? (b) What three things should he know before acting? (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'साधयेत्'. (d) What value does the heron teach?
questions.answer: (a) He should control his senses (इन्द्रियाणि). (b) He should know place, time and his own strength (देश, काल, बल). (c) साधयेत् = 'should accomplish'. (d) Value: self-control, concentration, and acting at the right place and time.
questions.explanation: Comprehension on the heron's self-control and timing.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
सिंहादेकं बकादेकं शिक्षेच्चत्वारि कुक्कुटात्।
वायसात् पञ्च शिक्षेच्च षट् शुनस्त्रीणि गर्दभात्॥
(a) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'शिक्षेच्चत्वारि'. (b) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'शुनस्त्रीणि'. (c) In which विभक्ति is 'वायसात्'? (d) How many qualities are listed in all?
questions.answer: (a) शिक्षेच्चत्वारि = शिक्षेत् + चत्वारि. (b) शुनस्त्रीणि = शुनः + त्रीणि. (c) वायसात् is पञ्चमी (ablative) — 'from the crow'. (d) Twenty qualities in all (1+1+4+5+6+3).
questions.explanation: Comprehension focused on sandhi splits and the ablative case.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
प्रत्युत्थानं च युद्धं च संविभागं च बन्धुषु।
स्वयमाक्रम्य भुक्तं च शिक्षेच्चत्वारि कुक्कुटात्॥
(a) Name any two qualities of the cock. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'बन्धुषु'. (c) How many qualities are learned from the cock? (d) What lesson does the cock teach a student?
questions.answer: (a) Any two of: alert rising at the right time (प्रत्युत्थानम्), courage in a fight (युद्धम्), sharing food with kinsmen (संविभागम्), and eating what one earns by one's own effort. (b) बन्धुषु = among kinsmen/relatives. (c) Four qualities (चत्वारि). (d) Lesson: be punctual, brave, generous with family, and earn honestly.
questions.explanation: Comprehension on the cock's four qualities.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
सिंहादेकं बकादेकं शिक्षेच्चत्वारि कुक्कुटात्।
वायसात् पञ्च शिक्षेच्च षट् शुनस्त्रीणि गर्दभात्॥
(a) Translate 'बकादेकम्'. (b) How many qualities are learned from the crow? (c) How many from the dog? (d) What is the overall message of the verse?
questions.answer: (a) बकादेकम् = 'one (quality) from the heron'. (b) Five from the crow. (c) Six from the dog. (d) Message: a wise person should gather good qualities from every source, learning twenty virtues from six creatures.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: translation, counts, and message.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
बह्वाशी स्वल्पसन्तुष्टः सुनिद्रो लघुचेतनः।
स्वामिभक्तश्च शूरश्च षडेते श्वानतो गुणाः॥
(a) In which विभक्ति is 'श्वानतः' (from the dog)? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'गुणाः'. (c) What does the number 'षट्' mean? (d) In which mood is the implied verb शिक्षेत्?
questions.answer: (a) श्वानतः shows the source, the पञ्चमी (ablative) sense 'from the dog' (formed with the ending -तः). (b) गुणाः = qualities/virtues. (c) षट् = six. (d) शिक्षेत् is in the विधिलिङ् (mood of 'should/ought').
questions.explanation: Comprehension on case, vocabulary, number and verb mood.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
सुश्रान्तोऽपि वहेद्भारं शीतोष्णं न च पश्यति।
सन्तुष्टश्चरते नित्यं त्रीणि शिक्षेच्च गर्दभात्॥
(a) Translate 'त्रीणि शिक्षेच्च गर्दभात्'. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'सन्तुष्टः'. (c) Does the donkey mind cold and heat? (d) What is the moral?
questions.answer: (a) 'And three (qualities) one should learn from the donkey.' (b) सन्तुष्टः = content/satisfied. (c) No — शीतोष्णं न च पश्यति, it does not mind cold or heat. (d) Moral: learn perseverance, endurance and contentment from the humble donkey.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: translation, vocabulary, endurance, moral.
